title: Lesson 6: Number Splitting
subtopics: Addition by splitting into two easy chunks
Choosing the split line to avoid carries
Division by splitting into two sections
Division with three sections and longer numbers
learningGoals: Split a long calculation into smaller mental chunks.
Choose split points that reduce carries, borrowing, or awkward division.
Use number splitting across addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
coreIdeas: A split is useful only when each chunk becomes easier than the whole problem.
Read the chunk answers from left to right so place value stays correct.
When a quotient chunk needs two places, keep the zero instead of dropping it.

workedExamples.method: Split as 23/45 and 67/38. Add the right chunk 45 + 38 = 83, then add the left chunk 23 + 67 = 90. Read the answer as 9083.
Split as 54/54 and 17/26. Compute 54 - 26 = 28 and 54 - 17 = 37. Read the answer as 3728.
Split as 6/04. Multiply each chunk by 7: 6 × 7 = 42 and 04 × 7 = 28. Read the answer as 4228.
Split as 34/56. Divide each part by 2: 34 ÷ 2 = 17 and 56 ÷ 2 = 28. Read the answer as 1728.

starterPractice: Warm-up: split 2345 + 6738 after two digits and say the two chunk sums.
Guided: solve 5454 - 1726 by giving the right chunk first.
Independent: solve 612 / 6 and explain why the answer contains a zero.

screenplay.subtopic: Division with three sections and longer numbers
screenplay.teacherLine: When one split is not enough, we can split into three sections.
screenplay.checkpointPrompt: How does 24453 ÷ 3 become 8151 by three-part splitting?

screenplay.teacherLine: A larger divisor also works if the sections fit it: 391352 divided by 13 becomes 39, 13, and 52, giving 3, 1, and 04, so the answer is 30104.
screenplay.checkpointPrompt: How does 24453 ÷ 3 become 8151 by three-part splitting?
screenplay.fallbackHint: The last chunk needs the leading zero to hold two places.

screenplay.subtopic: Division with three sections and longer numbers
screenplay.teacherLine: Try 91827 divided by 3. Tell me the three chunk quotients before the full answer.
screenplay.checkpointPrompt: How does 24453 ÷ 3 become 8151 by three-part splitting?
screenplay.fallbackHint: 91 ÷ 3 = 30 remainder-free in this manual's splitting layout, then 82 ÷ 3 = 27 and 7 ÷ 3 = 09 by the given pattern.

screenplay.subtopic: Division with three sections and longer numbers
screenplay.teacherLine: Final checkpoint: solve 3814 divided by 2 and 21014 divided by 7 using splitting.
screenplay.checkpointPrompt: How does 24453 ÷ 3 become 8151 by three-part splitting?
screenplay.fallbackHint: Use the chunking that makes each division easy and keep every place.

teachingFlowStages.intent: Open with a hard-looking sum and make it smaller by drawing a split line on the board.
Explain how chunking preserves place value and why a good split avoids carries or awkward borrowing.
Model one worked example each from addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
Ask the learner for the next chunk result before the full answer is revealed.
Move from easy two-chunk questions to longer splits and zero-sensitive quotient cases.
Confirm that every chunk answer fits back into the full number correctly.
Require the learner to explain where the split line was chosen and why it helped.
